changed.title: Incomparable row neighborhoods force a two-gate row deletion or a single OR reader for every row
changed.statement:
∀ (n m s : ℕ) (G : Fin (n + 1) → Fin m → Bool),
  2 ≤ n →
  (∀ u v : Fin (n + 1), u ≠ v → ∃ c : Fin m, G u c = true ∧ G v c = false) →
  PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost G s →
  (∃ u : Fin (n + 1), ∃ t : ℕ, t + 2 ≤ s ∧
    PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun a c => G (u.succAbove a) c) t) ∨
  (∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ C.size ≤ s ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n + 1 + m) C ∧
    PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C ∧
    ∀ u : Fin (n + 1),
      PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.readsIn C (Finset.range C.size) u.val = 1 ∧
      ∃ (j : Fin C.gates.length) (w : ℕ),
        (C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or ∧
        ((C.gates.get j).inputs = [u.val, w] ∨ (C.gates.get j).inputs = [w, u.val]))
changed.unlocks: the case split of the count of names against literals on the one-a-side promise: delete a row at two gates or every row feeds one OR; it joins the deletion step to the general count
changed.context: On paper. Fold constants, missing reads and repeated operands. Prune gates outside the output cone. If row u were unread, choose a column met by u and missed by v. Turning u off preserves output one and turning v on cannot lower it. Set u off if two gates read it: each folds away. If only an AND reads u, that AND becomes zero and one later reader folds too. It has a reader because another row has an edge. Renumber the survivors in order. In the remaining case each row occurs once at a binary OR with distinct operands. Companions cannot exist: it is about every graph.

changed.title: The 5 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 7865809 is represented on the one-a-side promise by an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 10 gates
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 10 ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 5 => (7865809 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) C
changed.unlocks: Whether a NOT gate pays under a checked AND/OR floor of 11 on this side-5 graph, by leaving its classes of equal rows or columns unread.
changed.sketch: We hold no circuit of 10 gates; this is a search. This graph has a class of 2 equal columns, which a circuit with NOT gates may leave unread. Give a gate list of AND, OR and NOT gates of fan-in two, at most 10 gates, judged by evaluation on the 25 promise inputs. The graph needs at least 11 AND/OR gates by a checked floor row (search 'mask 7865809'). An exhausted search is a report, not a proof.

changed.title: Binary encoder on 16 one-hot inputs: some AND/OR circuit of at most 21 gates, fan-in at most two, has all four bit wires
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ C.size ≤ 21 ∧ ∀ v : Fin 4, ∃ w : ℕ, ∀ p : Fin 16, (C.wires (List.ofFn (fun q : Fin 16 => decide (q = p)))).getD w false = Nat.testBit p.val v.val
changed.unlocks: a smaller circuit for the layer that turns one-hot inputs into index bits, which every representing bound of ours is measured against
changed.context: A calibration of our constructions; no claim attached either way. Answer with a gate list of AND and OR gates of fan-in two and the four bit wires, judged on the 16 one-hot inputs. We hold 22 gates (checked). With OR gates only, on 14 of the inputs, at least 20 are needed (checked). The room left is small; the truth is unknown to us. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 39262 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 10 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 4) (v : Fin 5) => (39262 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) 10
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 4 by 5 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 11 AND/OR gates (three plain forms, full lines taken out and equal gates merged); at this size those forms are weak; we hold none of 10; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 8 (on paper), a gap of 3. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 3 left, 4 to 8 right, gate j writes wire 9 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 20 inputs with one vertex on each side.
